spec: Write a function that treats a list of numbers as weights placed at positions 0, 1, 2, and so on, and computes the weighted average position (the sum of index times value, divided by the sum of the values), rounded to the nearest integer using standard Python rounding. Return -1 if the sum of the values is zero.

Given a list of dicts, return a sorted list of the keys that appear in exactly two of the dicts in the list (counting a key once per dict it appears in). An empty list, or one with no such keys, returns an empty list.

Group the integers in nums by how many digits their absolute value has (e.g. 0 and -9 both have 1 digit, 100 has 3 digits). Return a dict mapping each digit count to a sorted list of the numbers with that many digits. An empty list returns an empty dict.
Given a list of integers, sort them ascending by absolute value. When two numbers have the same absolute value, the negative one comes before the positive one. An empty list returns an empty list.
